checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (224 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is listed as [running/confirm] on equal footing with the other confirm arms, and the checklist reports '5 running' with no qualification.
findings.problem: entry-8pct has live_n=5 and screen_n=498 against control's screen_n=1560 and live_n=23, with declined=79 versus 47 for the rest. At 5 resolved live trades against a planned confirm n=600 it is contributing essentially nothing, yet it occupies one of the six mechanism-class slots and consumes one of the 6 lifetime tests that set alpha=0.00833. Its screen_ev is also -0.035, already negative. Reporting it as a peer of hold-12h (live_n=26) overstates how much of the arena is actually accumulating evidence.

findings.claim: 'paired_population: Every arm scored on identical events — 4848 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them' is green.
findings.problem: Seeing the same detections is not the same as being scored on the same events, which is what the title claims. The screen_n values differ materially across arms — control 1560, hold-12h 1563, tp-7pct 1556, vol-4x 874, entry-8pct 498 — so vol-4x and entry-8pct are scored on roughly half and a third of the population respectively, because their changed parameters are filters that decline events (declined=59 and 79 versus 47). A paired comparison of entry-8pct against control is therefore over a self-selected subset, not the shared 4848. The check as worded is green for a reason that does not establish the property it names.

findings.claim: Every screen row quotes screen_wr and screen_dWR to three decimals — e.g. sl-5pct screen_wr=55.385, screen_dWR=5.26pp — as if these were arm verdicts.
findings.problem: These are backfill-tier numbers (events by tier: backfill 4764 versus live 84), and the methodology forbids a lower tier outranking a higher one while backfill_cannot_promote confirms no arm may promote on them. No screen row carries a p-value or a comparison against alpha=0.00833, and none is labelled as screening-only in the arena display. Three-decimal precision on a backfill statistic invites exactly the ACC/MT reading the project has been burned by before.

findings.claim: hold-12h screen_dWR=3.27pp and sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.26pp are presented as deltas versus control.
findings.problem: Control's own screen row reports screen_dWR=0.0pp, so the deltas are anchored to control as required — but entry-8pct, placebo and vol-4x all also report screen_dWR=0.0pp despite screen_wr values of 51.807, 50.128 and 51.487 against control's 50.128. Only placebo's zero is arithmetically consistent. For entry-8pct and vol-4x the field is reporting 0.0pp where the arm's own quoted win rate differs from control's, so the delta column is not computed the same way for every arm and cannot be read across rows.

findings.claim: 'placebo_inert: Placebo is provably inert — control n=1560 WR=50.1 · placebo n=1560 WR=50.1 · discordant pairs b=0 c=0' is green and critical.
findings.problem: min_price=1e-12 is a no-op by construction on any positive price, so b=0/c=0 is guaranteed by arithmetic rather than measured. The check therefore establishes that the scoring pipeline is deterministic and reproducible, which is worth having, but it does not establish what a placebo is for: that an inert-but-non-trivial change produces no spurious signal. It is green for a weaker reason than its title claims, and it still consumes one of the six mechanism-class slots (liquidity_filter, shared with vol-4x).

findings.claim: 'kernel_agreement: Kernel finds the same setups as the live bot — 219/224 live setups reproduced (97.8%)' is green and critical.
findings.problem: The 224 matched setups are checked against events by tier showing only 84 live events, so the comparison population is not the live tape the promotion rule depends on. The same block also declares the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average because it enters at the hourly close while the bot scans every 5 min — a systematic entry-price difference in the direction that flatters a short. entry_granularity_declared correctly flags that arena absolute WR is not live WR, but the +0.54pp offset is not neutral across arms: entry-8pct gates on pump_pct=8.0, so a kernel that systematically reads pumps larger admits events the live bot would decline, and that arm's declined=79 is measured under the inflated reading.
